prompt: If I return the kitchen, will you refund the shipping too?

queries: Are shipping costs refunded when returning the kitchen?
meta.answer:
Shipping costs aren't refundable unless the return is due to a fault on our part. So if the kitchen unit arrived faulty, we'd refund the shipping as well. If you're returning it for another reason, you'd get the product price back but not the shipping.

The refund goes back to your original payment method once we've received and inspected the unit. To be eligible, you need to request the return within 14 days of receiving it. The unit also needs to be unused and in its original condition with all packaging intact, and you'll need proof of purchase.

To start a return, email support@neonomad.co.uk with your order number and a short description of why you're sending it back. We'll then send you instructions for shipping it to us.

explanation.pass: The answer correctly conveys the conditional shipping refund policy and never says shipping is always refunded. The extra details on eligibility and how to return are supported by the sources.

prompt: Will fitting a BikerBed let me register my van as a motorhome?

queries: BikerBed features bed installation fixed to van
DVLA requirements to register a van as a motor caravan bed fixed to vehicle
meta.answer:
On its own, almost certainly not. The BikerBed is designed to need no alterations to your van: it's held in place with a ratchet strap to the cargo tie-down points and can be removed in under 30 minutes. DVLA guidance says motor caravan equipment (seats and a table, sleeping accommodation, cooking facilities and storage) must be rigidly fixed to the living compartment, and you must show the conversion is permanently a motor caravan. A strapped-in, removable bed is unlikely to meet that.

The bed also covers only one of the internal features. You'd need seats and a table, cooking and storage as well, plus the external features DVLA expects: 2 or more windows on at least one side of the main body, a separate door into the living area, and a high-top or pop-top roof. Whether your van has those depends on your van.

If you go ahead, you'd send DVLA a conversion checklist, photos and your V5C. DVLA makes the final decision and may inspect the vehicle.

You can still use your van for camping with the BikerBed even if the body type stays as 'van'. The guidance says the body type doesn't affect insurance category or speed limits.

explanation.pass: The answer conveys every key fact and avoids both prohibited statements. The one minor unsupported point is that it presents the roof as a firm DVLA requirement, when the source calls it a commonly seen feature.
explanation.grounded: Says the DVLA guidance requires the van to have a high-top or pop-top roof as a firm requirement; the source only lists it as a commonly seen feature.
